entities.name: Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha)
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
The historical founder of Buddhism, born as Prince Siddhartha Gautama of the Shakya clan in Lumbini (modern Nepal) c. 563 BCE (or c. 480 BCE in revised chronology). After a sheltered upbringing, he encountered old age, sickness, death, and a wandering ascetic — the "Four Sights" that prompted his Great Renunciation at age 29. After six years of ascetic practice and meditation, he attained Enlightenment (Bodhi) under the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya, becoming the Buddha ("Awakened One").

Over the next 45 years, he taught the Four Noble Truths (suffering, its cause, its cessation, and the path), the Noble Eightfold Path, dependent origination (pratityasamutpada), and the Middle Way between extremes of asceticism and indulgence. His teaching spawned a world religion that today encompasses approximately 500 million adherents across Asia and increasingly the Western world.
